input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 imposes full-term sole-supplier exclusivity on us for hosted analytics services with no category or duration limit and no performance-based exit, which is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback (category-specific, 12 months, terminating on service level or delivery failure). It also conflicts with Section 2.1 (no minimum quantity or purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity commitment). The redline moves the clause to the preferred position by making Vendor a non-exclusive provider and confirming our freedom to source from third parties.

ops.oldText: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
ops.newText: Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services, and Customer may procure the same or similar services from any third party at any time.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made Vendor a non-exclusive provider, as our playbook does not permit sole-supplier obligations on us and we must retain freedom to source elsewhere. This also removes the conflict with Sections 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and 12.3 (no exclusivity commitment); if Vendor needs some protection we could discuss a category-specific exclusivity capped at 12 months that ends automatically on any service level or delivery failure.
proposal.summary: Convert Vendor's sole and exclusive provider status to non-exclusive.
